diffs.diff: co2_ppm: datasheet reading gives 1 per count, the part's model has none
diffs.evidence: Senseair TDE2067 rev 6 (Modbus on Senseair S8), p.15 'Sensor status and CO2 read sequence': 'We assume in this example that by sensor measured CO2 value is 400ppm ... Sensor replies with status=0 and CO2 value 400ppm (0x190 hexadecimal). Master Transmit: <FE> <04> <00> <00> <00> <04> <E5> <C6> Slave Reply: <FE> <04> <08> <00> <00> <00> <00> <00> <00> <01> <90> <16> <E6>'. 0x0190 = 400, so IR4 'Space CO2' (p.5) is 1 ppm per count, offset 0. The footnote says only 'some future models' divide by 10; the 004-0-0053 being modelled is the standard 1:1 unit. The model already uses this scale: sim.uartReplies has the CO2 segment {control:'value', bits:16, scale:1}, the driver returns the raw IR4 word as ppm, and the example test (slider 1234 -> 'CO2=1234 ppm') passes. The gate reports 'none' only because its authorConversions() reads sim.measure/sim.responses and not sim.uartReplies, which the uart-device kind uses.
